steal.headline: {company} investigates possible data leak
steal.body:
{CITY}. {company} said on {weekday} it was looking into 'irregular access' to its systems after staff found files had been opened overnight. The firm would not say what was taken.

A spokesperson said customers had 'no immediate cause for concern', and declined to answer further questions.

steal.headline: Copies of {company} files offered for sale, sources say
steal.body:
{CITY}. Documents that appear to come from {company} are being passed around online, according to two people who say they have seen them.

The company did not confirm a breach. 'We are aware of the claims,' it said in a short statement.

steal.headline: {company}: 'nothing of value' taken in break-in
steal.body:
{CITY}. {company} insisted that an intruder who reached its records this week left with 'nothing of value', a claim one former employee called 'optimistic'.

The firm has asked its staff not to discuss the matter with the press.

steal.headline: Ledger copied from {company}, regulator told
steal.body:
{CITY}. {company} has told the regulator that a copy of a confidential ledger left its network without permission. It is the second notice of its kind filed in {city} this quarter.

Customers are being advised to watch their statements.

steal.headline: {company} confirms files 'accessed without permission'
steal.body:
{CITY}. {company} confirmed on {weekday} that files were opened by someone with no right to them. It said the matter was in the hands of its lawyers.

'We take the privacy of our work extremely seriously,' a spokesperson said, in the tone of a person who has said it before.

steal.headline: Staff at {company} told to change every password
steal.body: {CITY}. An email seen by the Wire tells employees of {company} to change every password by the end of the day and not to say why. Several said they had heard rumours of a copy of internal files going elsewhere.

steal.headline: What did the intruder take from {company}?
steal.body: {CITY}. Nobody at {company} can say what left the building this week, only that something did. 'The logs are very polite,' one engineer said. 'They show exactly who looked, and it was nobody.'

steal.headline: Patient lists copied at {company}, clinic confirms
steal.body:
{CITY}. {company} has written to patients to say that a list of names was copied from its systems. No treatment records are thought to be involved, though the clinic said it could not be sure.

A helpline has been opened.

steal.headline: Pupil records copied from {company}
steal.body: {CITY}. Parents of children at {company} are being told that a copy of its register was taken from the school's network. The head said the school was 'working with the authorities and with our own IT volunteer'.

steal.headline: Designs leaked from {company}, rivals circle
steal.body: {CITY}. Drawings that look like they come from {company} are said to be in the hands of at least two competitors. The company says its designs are 'protected in many ways' and declined to list them.

steal.headline: Customer list from {company} said to be on sale
steal.body: {CITY}. A list of customers of {company} is being offered for sale, according to a post that vanished within the hour. The firm said it had no comment 'at this time', which analysts took to mean 'later'.

destroy.headline: {company} loses records in 'catastrophic' failure
destroy.body:
{CITY}. Staff at {company} arrived on {weekday} to find a set of records gone from its systems. The firm first blamed a faulty disk, then 'an outside party'.

Backups are being checked. One manager described the mood in the office as 'grim'.

destroy.headline: Weeks of work wiped at {company}
destroy.body:
{CITY}. A file holding weeks of work vanished from {company}'s network overnight. Engineers are trying to rebuild it from paper copies.

'Someone knew exactly what to delete,' one member of staff said.

destroy.headline: Community business loses a year of billing
destroy.body:
{CITY}. {company} says a year of billing records has been erased, leaving it unable to say who owes what. Customers have been asked to keep their receipts.

The local council has offered help with the paperwork.

destroy.headline: {company} 'rebuilding from scratch' after data loss
destroy.body: {CITY}. {company} says it is restoring its {records} by hand after a deletion it cannot yet explain. Customers have been asked for patience and, in some cases, for copies of their own paperwork.

destroy.headline: Backups failed too, {company} admits
destroy.body: {CITY}. When {company} lost a file this week, staff reached for the backup. It was damaged as well. 'Not by accident,' said a source, 'someone had been through it first.'

destroy.headline: Fire drill or sabotage? {company} cannot say
destroy.body: {CITY}. {company} said on {weekday} that a file central to its work was deleted overnight. An internal memo calls the loss 'significant but recoverable'. Staff say it is neither.

destroy.headline: Case files gone at {company}
destroy.body: {CITY}. {company} is asking clients to resend documents after a set of case files vanished from its network. A partner said the firm had 'not yet established' whether the loss was deliberate.

destroy.headline: Clinic loses appointment book
destroy.body: {CITY}. {company} has gone back to pen and paper after its appointment records were wiped. Patients are being phoned one by one. Urgent cases are being seen first.

record.headline: {company} finds records 'quietly changed'
record.body:
{CITY}. An internal check at {company} found that at least one entry in its {records} had been altered by an account that should not have had access.

The firm said it had 'restored the correct figures', and would not say who benefited.

record.headline: Questions over figures at {company}
record.body: {CITY}. {company} has paused a review of its {records} after an auditor noticed a change nobody could explain. The company called it 'a clerical error under investigation'.

record.headline: {company} corrects 'a small error' in its {records}
record.body: {CITY}. {company} has issued a correction to its {records}, saying a figure had been 'entered wrongly'. Two former employees told the Wire that the figure was right until Tuesday.

record.headline: Who changed the figures at {company}?
record.body: {CITY}. An account at {company} edited a record at three in the morning, then logged out. The account belongs to someone who was on holiday. 'Someone borrowed them,' a colleague said.

read.headline: {company} reports 'unusual activity' on its network
read.body:
{CITY}. {company} said someone spent time inside its network this week, but that as far as it could tell nothing was taken or changed.

'They looked,' said one technician. 'That is somehow worse.'

read.headline: {company} finds someone read its files, took nothing
read.body: {CITY}. An audit at {company} shows an outside party opened a long list of files this week and changed none of them. 'It was a visit, not a robbery,' the firm said, and asked that nobody read anything into it.

read.headline: Quiet visitor in {company}'s network
read.body: {CITY}. For the better part of an afternoon, someone moved through the systems of {company} without disturbing a thing. Staff only noticed when a log was read back to front. 'Considerate,' said one, dryly.

plant.headline: Mystery file found on {company} server
plant.body: {CITY}. Staff at {company} have found a file on the company's server that none of them put there. The firm has handed it to its lawyers and will not say what it contains.

plant.headline: {company} finds file it did not write
plant.body: {CITY}. An unfamiliar file was found on a server at {company} this week. The firm's security staff said it was 'being examined'. One technician said it was 'oddly neat'.

plant.headline: Strange upload at {company} baffles IT
plant.body: {CITY}. IT staff at {company} are trying to work out how a new file reached their server, and why. 'Nobody has asked for it, nobody will claim it,' the head of IT said.

frame.headline: {company} names suspect after break-in
frame.body: {CITY}. {company} says its logs point at a single address, and that it has passed the details to the police. Friends of the person named say they have never heard of the company.

frame.headline: Police question man over {company} break-in
frame.body: {CITY}. A man has been questioned about a break-in at {company}, after its logs showed a connection from his address. His lawyer said he 'does not own a computer that works'.

frame.headline: Break-in at {company}: logs 'point one way'
frame.body: {CITY}. {company} says there is no doubt who is responsible. A neighbour of the man named said he is 'a quiet type, mostly interested in fishing'.

caught.headline: Intrusion at {company} traced, police called
caught.body:
{CITY}. {company} said its security staff followed an intruder's connection back through several countries this week before it was cut off. The firm has passed what it found to the police.

'Whoever it was will think twice,' said a manager.

caught.headline: {company} says it 'saw off' an attack
caught.body: {CITY}. {company} claims its systems detected and traced a break-in attempt within minutes. It is not known whether anyone has been identified.

caught.headline: {company} traces intruder to a relay in {country}
caught.body: {CITY}. {company} said its security staff followed a connection through four servers before it dropped. 'We know where to look now,' said the head of security. 'That is half of knowing who.'

caught.headline: Security team at {company} 'won the race'
caught.body: {CITY}. {company} says its monitoring cut off an intruder this week with seconds to spare. The firm is expected to use the episode in its next advertising.

caught.headline: Hackers 'do not get a second chance' at {company}
caught.body: {CITY}. After an intrusion was traced and cut off, {company} announced a review of its security. 'Everyone makes mistakes,' its director said. 'We do not plan to make this one again.'

guard.headline: {company} says it fought off a determined attack
guard.body: {CITY}. {company} says an intruder spent the best part of an hour trying to break into its network this week, and failed. 'Someone was watching the door,' a manager said, without saying who.

guard.headline: Night attack on {company} 'went nowhere'
guard.body: {CITY}. {company} confirmed that someone tried the doors of its network for most of an evening and got nothing. A technician credited 'a very lucky coincidence' that a hand was on the switch.

guard.headline: {company} thanks a stranger
guard.body: {CITY}. A message from a stranger warned {company} an attack was coming, and then, according to one source, helped to repel it. The company said it did not know who to thank.

hold.headline: Long intrusion at {company} puzzles staff
hold.body: {CITY}. Staff at {company} watched an unknown connection sit inside their network for several minutes this week, doing nothing they could see. 'It was like someone holding a door,' said one.

hold.headline: Unknown session sits in {company}'s systems for minutes
hold.body: {CITY}. {company} reported an unknown session that stayed connected, silent and apparently idle, until it was cut off. 'Whatever it was waiting for, it got it,' a manager said.

hunt.headline: Trail through {company} leads to a hacker's machine
hunt.body: {CITY}. Logs at {company} have helped someone follow a hacker's route back to the machine it came from, according to a post on an underground board. The company says it was not consulted.

hunt.headline: Trail from {company} 'led all the way home', hacker claims
hunt.body: {CITY}. Someone has posted a screenshot suggesting that logs at {company} were used to follow a hacker's connection back to its source. Police said they were 'not part of that exercise'.

swap.headline: Doubts over figures held by {company}
swap.body: {CITY}. A document held by {company} says something different this week from what several people remember it saying. The company insists the file has not been touched.

swap.headline: Which version is real? Document dispute at {company}
swap.body: {CITY}. Two people at {company} remember a document saying different things. The file on the server is the only record, and it says what the newer person remembers. The older person has been moved to another department.

swap.headline: {company} 'stands by' its paperwork
swap.body: {CITY}. {company} rejected suggestions that a file in its records had been replaced, calling the claims 'fantasy'. It declined to let anyone compare the file with an earlier copy.

guard.headline: {company} tightens security after break-in
guard.body: {CITY}. {company} says it has strengthened its {layer} for the coming days while it investigates. Staff were asked to change their passwords.

guard.headline: {company} on alert
guard.body: {CITY}. Following recent trouble, {company} has put extra watch on its network. 'We are taking no chances,' a spokesperson said.

guard.headline: {company} puts extra eyes on the {layer}
guard.body: {CITY}. After a recent intrusion, {company} has doubled the watch on its {layer}. Staff described the change as 'sensible', and also as 'a lot of paperwork'.

guard.headline: Week of 'heightened vigilance' at {company}
guard.body: {CITY}. {company} told staff it will treat every odd connection as an attack for the next few days. It has also asked them to stop plugging in things they find in the car park.

firm.headline: {company} hires security firm after third breach
firm.body:
{CITY}. After a third incident in a short space of time, {company} has signed a contract with an outside security firm. Its network will be watched around the clock.

'Enough is enough,' said the managing director.

firm.headline: {company} brings in outside guards for its network
firm.body: {CITY}. Three breaches in quick succession have convinced {company} to hire a security firm to watch its systems night and day. 'We should have done it years ago,' a director said. 'We were told, often.'

events.headline: {company} agrees to merge with {company2}
events.body: {CITY}. {company} and {company2} of {city2} have agreed to combine. Staff were told the move would be 'seamless'. Both firms' systems are to be joined in the coming weeks, and IT staff are said to be stretched.

events.headline: Outage takes {company} offline
events.body: {CITY}. {company} spent most of {weekday} offline after what it called 'a fault in a supplier's equipment'. Engineers are working through the backlog with security checks switched off to save time.

events.headline: {company} cuts staff, including IT
events.body: {CITY}. {company} has let go of a fifth of its staff, among them two of the three people who looked after its network. A union representative said the remaining team was 'already overwhelmed'.

events.headline: Auditors called in at {company}
events.body: {CITY}. Outside auditors will spend the next fortnight at {company}, according to a notice sent to staff. Some at the firm would rather certain files were not found.

events.headline: {company} wins regional business award
events.body: {CITY}. {company} was named one of {country}'s most promising firms at a dinner on {weekday} night. Its director thanked 'a team that never cuts corners'.

events.headline: {company} sued by former client
events.body: {CITY}. A former client is suing {company}, claiming the firm lost papers it was paid to keep. The company says it will 'defend itself vigorously'.

events.headline: Police in {city} arrest hacker known as '{handle}'
events.body:
{CITY}. Police have arrested a man they say worked online under the name '{handle}'. Officers seized several computers. Investigators say his connections were bounced through 'dozens' of servers, some of them in {country}.

He has not been charged.

events.headline: Hacker '{handle}' released without charge
events.body: {CITY}. A suspect known online as '{handle}' has been released, after prosecutors said they could not show which of the many relays in his route had actually been his. Police called the result 'frustrating'.

events.headline: Open relays 'a gift to criminals', says minister
events.body: {CITY}. A minister in {country} has called for public relays to be registered and watched. The Open Relay Foundation said the plan 'would not stop a single crime and would end a great deal of privacy'.

events.headline: Undersea cable repair slows traffic across the {ocean}
events.body: A repair ship is working on a damaged cable on the floor of the {ocean}. Engineers expect traffic between the continents to be slow, and some routes to be watched more closely, until the work is finished.

events.headline: Night shift at {company} walks out
events.body: {CITY}. The night shift at {company} stopped work on {weekday}, citing pay and conditions. Managers are covering the network themselves, which is not what they were hired for.

events.headline: {company} rushes a software upgrade
events.body: {CITY}. {company} installed a new system this week, ahead of schedule and, according to staff, ahead of testing. Some checks are said to be disabled 'until the bugs are out'.

events.headline: Head of {company} steps down 'to spend time elsewhere'
events.body: {CITY}. The director of {company} resigned on {weekday}, with immediate effect and no explanation. Staff were told to expect 'continuity'. Three of them said they expected an inquiry.

events.headline: {company} moves offices, and servers
events.body: {CITY}. {company} is moving to new premises in {city}. During the move its records are being copied to a temporary system that, one engineer admitted, 'has a lock, in principle'.

events.headline: {company} reports record profits
events.body: {CITY}. {company} announced its best year on record on {weekday}. Its director put the result down to 'hard work and, frankly, discretion'.

events.headline: {company} recalls a product after complaints
events.body: {CITY}. {company} has recalled one of its products. A leaked memo suggests the firm knew about the fault long before the first complaint, which the company called 'a misreading'.

events.headline: Power cut in {city} knocks out {company}
events.body: {CITY}. A power failure left {company} on backup supplies for most of {weekday}. Its monitoring system, according to a staff member, 'was one of the things we turned off to save the batteries'.

events.headline: New data rules in {country} 'unworkable', say firms
events.body: {CITY}. Companies in {country} complained this week about a new law requiring them to report every break-in within three days. {company} called it 'a paperwork tax'. Security researchers said it would make firms more honest, in time.

events.headline: {company} advertises for a 'security analyst, junior'
events.body: {CITY}. {company} is looking for a junior security analyst, and the advertisement is unusually long. Industry watchers say it reads like a list of things the firm has recently lost.

events.headline: {company} fined over lost data
events.body: {CITY}. A regulator fined {company} this week for losing customer data last year, a case that took two years and one change of lawyers to settle. The company said it 'has learned from the experience'.

story.headline: Payment network 'answered itself', engineers say
story.body:
ZURICH. A clearing network that handles payments between six banks briefly began replying to its own test messages on Tuesday night, its engineers say. No money moved.

'It is a loop somewhere,' said one. 'We will find it.'

story.headline: Sleep clinic volunteers describe 'the same dream'
story.body: OSLO. Several volunteers in an unregistered sleep study say they woke describing an identical grey room. A psychologist told the Wire it was 'a well-known effect of suggestion'.

story.headline: Night traffic on public relays doubles, nobody knows why
story.body: The Open Relay Foundation says traffic through public relays between two and five in the morning has doubled in a month. Most of it goes nowhere at all. 'It looks like someone testing every door in the building,' its chair said.

story.headline: Unscheduled network test puzzles telecoms firm
story.body: A telecoms operator reported a burst of traffic with no source and no purpose on Thursday. 'It tested the same fifty doors, politely, and left,' an engineer said. The company is treating it as 'a fault'.

story.headline: Records clerk's complaint 'went missing', union says
story.body: A union representative says a clerk filed a complaint about a research project last spring, and that the complaint has since disappeared from the files. The clerk could not be reached.

story.headline: Gateway makers warn of 'curious customers'
story.body: A manufacturer of home gateways has told retailers to expect a rise in returns from customers who say their hardware 'knows when it is being watched'. The company said it was a software matter.

story.headline: Radio hams report voices on a dead frequency
story.body: Amateur radio operators in three countries say they heard something like speech on a frequency nobody has used for years. A regulator said it was 'almost certainly interference'.

story.headline: Reinsurer denies 'claims desk for special cases'
story.body: Calder Reinsurance has rejected claims that it keeps a desk for matters it would rather not discuss. 'We keep many desks,' a spokesperson said. 'Each of them is for ordinary business.'

story.headline: Ghent grid "running better than ever", operator says
story.body: GHENT. The operator of the city's power grid says its network has not tripped once in six weeks, a record. Asked what changed, a spokesperson said that "a number of small things were put right overnight" and that nobody on staff could say by whom.

story.headline: Grid operator puzzled by "maintenance" nobody scheduled
story.body: A software tool appeared on the control system of a Belgian grid operator this week and was found to be doing exactly what the operator wanted. The operator has asked a government office to explain. The office declined to comment.

story.headline: Break-in at forecasting annex "found nothing missing"
story.body: THE HAGUE. Officials say a facility used by a forecasting directorate was entered overnight but that nothing was taken. "The only change was a line in the access log," a spokesperson said. A reinsurer's liaison was seen at the annex the following week.

story.headline: Lisbon publisher withstands two nights of attack
story.body: LISBON. A small publishing collective says its site was under sustained attack for two nights and that it stayed up. The collective says it will publish "within days". It would not say what.

story.headline: Three cities report a night without a single fault
story.body: For the first time on record, three mid-sized cities reported no outage, no failed payment and no late train in a single night. Officials called it "a statistical curiosity". A commuter told the Wire it had been "a bit creepy, honestly".

weather: Rain over the North Sea, clearing by evening.
Fog in the Channel ports. Flights out of {city} delayed.
A cold front across the Baltic, snow on high ground.
Heat warning for southern Europe; data centres asked to save power.
Storms in the Bay of Bengal. Shipping told to stay in port.
Clear skies over most of the Americas.
Monsoon rain in Mumbai, flooding in low streets.
A dry, windy day across the Cape.
Thunder over the Alps, with rain by nightfall in {city}.
A warm, windy morning in {city}, turning grey by afternoon.
Sleet in northern Canada, mild elsewhere.
Dust over the Sahel; flights delayed at several airports.
A bright, still day across the Pacific coast.
Cool and wet in {city}. Nothing much expected from the sky or the markets.
Smog warning in several southern Asian cities.
Light snow in Scandinavia, heavier by the weekend.
